world: 03 — Monument (reference pole: experiment.obys.agency, measured 2026-07-26; all numbers below cite the "static anatomy" section of research/NOTES.md unless marked OURS)
policy: WHITE / NIGHT — a wry museum-label toggle: two 13px League Gothic caps words, active at 100% ink, idle at the 20% dim tier. It is NOT a palette fade: flipping it runs a literal gallery blackout — two ink curtains close power4.inOut 0.75s, the world flips at full cover, curtains part expo.inOut 0.9s (structural-wipe grammar straight from the measured vocabulary). WHAT FLIPS, surface by surface: page void #ffffff → #000000; ink #000000 → #ffffff; hairlines #0003 → rgba(255,255,255,0.2) (alpha constant 0.2, only the channel flips — the reference's own hairline alpha); dim tier rgba(0,0,0,0.2) → rgba(255,255,255,0.2); shader uniforms uWash and uFog vec3(1.0) → vec3(0.0) (whitewash → blackwash, distance-fog-to-white → fog-to-black); renderer clearColor #ffffff → #000000; preloader/blackout curtains black-on-white ↔ white-on-black; all drawn SVG glyphs flip free via currentColor. WHAT STAYS: every size, inset, ease, lerp constant, the 0.4 wash mix, grayscale-by-luminance stays ON in both modes (the reference's Pride kills it globally; our color reveal is local, via hover — the wittier move), the clock keeps ticking, the 32 textures are byte-identical. Day = lightbox (prints on white), Night = darkroom (slides in the dark). Reads localStorage 'hub-theme' ('day'|'night') synchronously in an inline head script pre-paint (day→White, night→Night, fallback prefers-color-scheme) so first paint is scheme-correct with zero animation; toggle writes the same key back — lab-wide continuity both directions. Rationale, one line: the reference proved the toggle should be a curatorial joke executed with two uniforms, not a settings panel — ours is the negative of the same photograph.
typecasting: ONE face, one weight — the reference's most radical move (OTF Obys NG 400 does their 94px and their 13px), so our utility face question answers itself: the single face IS the concept; a second family would be decoration. Cast: **League Gothic Regular 400** (SIL OFL 1.1, League of Movable Type) — Benton's Alternate Gothic No.1 revived; American wood-type condensed gothic, caps-forward, effectively single-weight, which makes the measured binary discipline a property of the file itself rather than a rule we enforce. Chosen over Khand (too calligraphic at 180px), Big Shoulders (too wide — its ancestry is civic signage, not wood type), and Anybody (variable width is a feature we'd set once and freeze — paying variable-file cost for a static decision). Roles, all measured from the pole: HERO 180px / lh 0.9 / ls −0.055em / uppercase — the escalation tier the reference declared and never used, deployed by us exactly once, on the monument itself; DISPLAY 94px / lh 0.9 / ls −0.055em / uppercase (section heads, Gift Shop); UTILITY 13px / ls −0.01em / uppercase (nav, clock, toggle, captions, table, footer) — condensed caps at 13px read as engraved plaque lettering, which IS the museum-label voice; DIM TIER 13px at 20% ink. The same face renders inside the 2D-canvas poster generator (await document.fonts.load('620px "League Gothic"') before generation) so the colossal numerals in the textures are set in the world's own type. NOT yet self-hosted (current site/public/fonts holds Cabinet Grotesk, Clash Display, General Sans, Outfit, Sometype Mono) → one download, below. Ship as site/public/fonts/LeagueGothic-Regular.woff2, preload in head, @font-face with font-display:block (the honest preloader counter covers the wait; no FOUT fallback face exists in a one-face world).

downloads.name: League Gothic Regular (single static weight, woff2)

sections.name: Frame & Preloader (fixed chrome)
sections.spec: **Grid law (page-wide, measured):** 10px page margin, 10px gaps, 12 equal columns; ALL fixed corner UI at 10px insets; caption band anchored at top: 226px. Colors: void #fff / ink #000 / hairline #0003 (Night: #000 / #fff / rgba(255,255,255,0.2)); dim tier = same 0.2-alpha value as the hairline, exactly per the pole. **Virtual-scroll skeleton (OURS, load-bearing):** the page is one translating DOM strip of 9 viewports, v ∈ [0,9]: hero [0,1) · Hall I formations [1,6] · strip pan [6,7] · The Index [7,8] · Colophon [8,9]. Wheel Δ·0.002 into target v (clamped 0–9), content translated with GSAP `set` + per-frame lerp 0.1 — no native scrollbar, the reference's hand-rolled inertia; ArrowUp/Down/Space/PageUp/PageDown add equivalent deltas (±0.05 / ±1.0). The WebGL canvas is position:fixed inset:0, z 0, pointer-events:none, always mounted; DOM strip z 1. Hero, Hall I and the strip-pan viewports have TRANSPARENT backgrounds (the washed gallery shows through); Index and Colophon sections carry background: var(--void) so the archival table reads clean. Canvas opacity per frame = 1 − smoothstep(6.8, 7.2, v_lerped) — it dissolves as The Index arrives and returns when you scroll back. **Corner UI, all 13px caps ls −0.01em:** - top-left: `03 — MONUMENT` + dim-tier second line `WING 03 OF 04` - top-right: toggle `WHITE / NIGHT` — active word 100% ink, idle 20%; idle-word hover lifts to 60% via CSS `color 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)` (color only — GSAP owns transforms); click runs the blackout (see policy). `

sections.name: Hero — Monument to the Unfinished
sections.spec:
First viewport (v ∈ [0,1)), transparent over the live Fibonacci-sphere formation (t clamped to 0 — the washed grayscale sphere hangs behind the type from first frame; whitewash 0.4 + fog keep the ink supreme). Centered stack, three lines at the single sanctioned 180px tier (lh 0.9 → 162px/line, ls −0.055em, uppercase):

`MONUMENT` / `TO THE` / `UNFINISHED`

(At the 1200px floor the longest line, 10 chars, measures ≈ 760px in League Gothic — fits with air.)

1px hairlines run FULL-BLEED (margin to margin) between the lines and above/below the stack; each display line pulls up into its rule with margin-top −7px — rules slice through letterforms, the measured grammar verbatim. Below the stack, a 13px utility row split to the margins: left `THE PLASTER NEVER SETS.` — right, dim tier: `PERMANENT COLLECTION — 32 EXHIBITS`.

**Entrance:** hairlines first — scaleX 0→1 from left, expo.out 1.0s, stagger 0.08 (GSAP, transform-owned); display lines reveal clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0) 0.5s power2.out, line stagger 0.08; utility row expo.out 0.8s delay 0.4. NO exit tween: the virtual scroll carries the hero off-screen naturally, which is what the reference's page does — an extra fade would be improvisation. The 180px tier appears exactly once in the world; everywhere else the scale is brutally binary (94/13).

sections.name: Hall I — The Permanent Collection (centerpiece stage)
sections.spec:
v ∈ [1,7): the fixed WebGL canvas IS this section (DOM is transparent here). Formation timeline parameter t = clamp((v−1)/5, 0, 1): t 0–0.2 SPHERE · 0.2–0.4 RING · 0.4–0.6 FLOWER · 0.6–0.75 CYLINDER · 0.75–1.0 morph to THE STRIP. Between formations the current formation label exits power2.in 0.4s and the next enters expo.out 0.8s. v ∈ [6,7]: strip pan — camera.x = (v−6.5)·124 world units (strip spans ±62), lerp 0.1, planes at identity rotation.

**Caption at top: 226px (measured anchor),** 13px, two lines, fixed while v ∈ [1,7]: `HALL I — THE PERMANENT COLLECTION` + dim: `NOTHING HERE IS RANDOM. EVERYTHING HERE IS SEEDED.` Fades out power2.in 0.4s as v crosses 6.8.

**Formation label,** bottom-center 13px, aria-live="polite": `FORMATION I — SPHERE (FIBONACCI, R 6.5)` → `FORMATION II — RING (JITTERED, R 5.2)` → `FORMATION III — FLOWER (GOLDEN ANGLE, 137.5°)` → `FORMATION IV — CYLINDER (R 4.2, TWO TURNS)` → `THE STRIP (SPACING 4)`.

Full scene recipe in centerpiece. prefers-reduced-motion: formation morphs become cuts (uOpacity snap), idle yaw off, entrances collapse to 0.3s fades.

sections.name: The Index
sections.spec:
v ∈ [7,8), solid void background (canvas has dissolved). Display head `THE INDEX` at 94px / lh 0.9 / ls −0.055em, one full-bleed hairline through it, margin-top −7px; reveal clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0) 0.5s power2.out on entry.

A 32-row archival table on the 12-col grid, row height 34px, 1px #0003 rules between rows, all cells 13px ls −0.01em caps. Columns: NO. (col 1) / SEED (cols 2–4) / PALETTE (cols 5–7) / SEAT — the exhibit's Fibonacci-sphere coordinate, rounded to 1 decimal (cols 8–10) / VIEW (cols 11–12). NO./SEED/SEAT at the dim tier; PALETTE and VIEW at full ink. Rows computed from the actual formula (y_k = 1−2(k+0.5)/32, θ_k = k·2.399963, r 6.5) — first three, exact:
`01 · 20260300 · NOIR · ( 1.6, 6.3, 0.0 ) · VIEW`
`02 · 20260301 · CHROME · ( −2.0, 5.9, 1.9 ) · VIEW`
`03 · 20260302 · MONUMENT · ( 0.3, 5.5, −3.5 ) · VIEW`
Row hover: dim cells lift to 100% via CSS `color 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)` (color only). Clicking VIEW sets the virtual-scroll target to center exhibit k in the strip: **v_target = 6.5 + (k−15.5)/31** (inverts camX = (v−6.5)·124 against strip x = (k−15.5)·4); the 0.1 scroll lerp does the glide — no tween, the reference's inertia IS the transition. Rows enter with 0.02 stagger, expo.out 0.8s, opacity + clip-path only (translate-free, GSAP).

sections.name: Colophon — the wall label
sections.spec:
Last viewport (v ∈ [8,9]), solid void, one hairline across the top. Left 6 columns: a museum wall label set entirely at 13px, labels dim / values ink, one hairline between entries:

`MONUMENT TO THE UNFINISHED, 2026`
`MEDIUM: SEEDED CANVAS ON WEBGL. ONE TYPEFACE. NO PHOTOGRAPHS.`
`DIMENSIONS: VARIABLE (MINIMUM 1200 × ANYTHING).`
`PROVENANCE: MADE HERE. ON LOAN FROM: NO ONE.`
`CONDITION: NEVER FINISHED, BY DESIGN.`
`TYPE: LEAGUE GOTHIC, SIL OPEN FONT LICENSE 1.1.` (license fact, not an acknowledgement ritual)

Right 6 columns, bottom-aligned: `NEXT WING: 04 — PULSE` (href /worlds/04-pulse/) and `BACK TO THE HUB` (href /), each preceded by the drawn hairline arrow; hover = arrow redraw 0.5s power2.out + color lift (CSS color-only 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)). Entrances expo.out 0.8s, block stagger 0.12.

sections.name: The Gift Shop (small-viewport treatment, <1200px)
sections.spec:
DECISION: mirror the pole's hard 1199px floor, never a dead end — the one hard idea here is architectural scale, and a miniaturized monument is a different (worse) idea; the hub is fully responsive, so nobody is stranded. Below 1200px the world serves a designed postcard card, centered on the 12-col grid, zero WebGL:

13px dim: `MUSEUM NOTICE` — then the 94px display as a FOUR-LINE stack (binary scale stays pure — a smaller size would counterfeit it): `THE` / `MONUMENT` / `DOES NOT` / `TRAVEL`. Longest line 8 chars ≈ 315px in League Gothic at 94px — fits 320px viewports honestly, each line pulls up into its hairline with margin-top −7px. Then 13px: `THIS HALL IS HUNG AT ARCHITECTURAL SCALE — 1200 PIXELS OF IT, MINIMUM. UNTIL THEN: A POSTCARD FROM THE GIFT SHOP.`

Below: ONE poster from the same generator rendered as a plain 2D canvas at 256×362 (exhibit index = dayOfYear % 32 — deterministic per date, 'postcard of the day'; role="img", aria-label `Exhibit NN, seeded poster`), framed by a 1px hairline with 10px inset, caption at dim tier: `EXHIBIT NN — SEED 202603NN`. WHITE/NIGHT toggle and BACK TO THE HUB remain fully functional; theme read pre-paint from 'hub-theme' exactly as on desktop.

assets2d: Two asset families, both built from what we own — no downloads, no stock, no AI gradient blobs. (1) THE POSTER GENERATOR — 32 deterministic exhibition posters, 2D canvas 512×724 (A-series ratio), rng = mulberry32(20260300 + i) for exhibit i ∈ 0–31 (seeds 20260300–20260331, printed in The Index — the seed is public curatorial data). Palette = PALETTES[i % 5] — the whole lab hiding inside the collection, every hex traceable to our own tokens or our measured poles: P0 NOIR {ground #f9f4eb, ink #1a1c1c, accents [#e75d60]} (lamalama measured); P1 CHROME {ground #eae9e6, ink #181818, accents [#ff4c24, #ecfdad, #3fae86]} (hildenkaira measured); P2 MONUMENT {ground #ffffff, ink #000000, accents [#ab54f7]} (our hub gate violet); P3 PULSE {ground #e5262c, ink #fdd2d2, accents [#3d3c47, #f9cfd1, #00b870]} (blood-donation measured — pink ink on red, the pole's own two-tone; a dark-on-red numeral would be mud); P4 HUB {ground #f4ebe0, ink #0e0d0b, accents [#0072e3, #ffb200, #ea3737]} (hub tokens verbatim). Paint order: (a) ground fill; (b) 3 horizontal 1px hairlines at y = round(724·rng()), ink at 20% alpha — the world's hairline grammar echoed inside the artwork; (c) n = 2 + floor(rng()·3) shapes from a 3-glyph grammar — disc, ring (14px stroke), full-bleed bar (horizontal if rng()<0.5, thickness (0.04+0.10·rng())·512) — radii (0.08+0.14·rng())·512, x snapped to the 12-column grid (col·512/12 — the page grid echoed), colors from palette accents in order, first shape alpha 1.0, others 0.3+0.4·rng(); (d) the colossal numeral String(i+1).padStart(2,'0') in 620px League Gothic, fill palette ink, alphabetic baseline y = 724·0.94, horizontally centered with manual −0.055em tracking (draw per char, advance = ctx.measureText(ch).width − 34px); bleeding off-canvas is allowed and monumental; (e) caption 18px League Gothic caps at ink 20%: `EXHIBIT NN — SEED 202603NN`, x 24, y 44. Await document.fonts.load('620px "League Gothic"') before generating (preloader points 20–84). CanvasTexture, colorSpace SRGB, anisotropy 4, LinearMipmapLinearFilter. The SAME generator feeds the WebGL planes, the rung-2 DOM strip, and the Gift Shop postcard — one recipe, three outputs, cache-stable everywhere (mulberry32, never Math.random). (2) DRAWN SVG GLYPHS in 1px hairline geometry (ASSETS.md icons-are-drawn rule; never Lucide): hairline arrow 24×8, a single 1px path (shaft + half-chevron head), draw-on via stroke-dasharray/offset 0.5s power2.out, used on BACK TO THE HUB and both colophon links; plinth square 8×8 1px outline as index-row bullet; the preloader's centered 1px line at 52.5% width is the third mark of the set. All glyph strokes use currentColor so the blackout flips them for free.
motion: Vocabulary lifted verbatim from the measured pole, then applied, never improvised. TWEENS (all GSAP): entrances expo.out 0.8–1.2s with staggers 0.02 (chars/rows) / 0.08 (lines) / 0.12 (blocks); text reveals clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0) 0.5s power2.out; exits power2.in 0.4s; structural moves (theme blackout curtains close/part 0.75s/0.9s power4.inOut + expo.inOut, preloader part expo.inOut 1.2s); hairline entrances scaleX expo.out 1.0s stagger 0.08. CSS MICRO-MOTION — color/filter/opacity ONLY, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) 0.3s (the measured CSS twin of expo.out): idle-toggle hover lift, index-row dim lift, rung-2 filter hover. GSAP owns element transforms exclusively — no transition:transform anywhere in the stylesheet. CONTINUOUS = per-frame lerp, not tweens: planes/camera 0.05, virtual-scroll inertia 0.1, cursor 0.15, uColor hover 0.15 in / 0.05 out (attention has inertia like everything else); wheel Δ·0.002. Canvas opacity vs scroll: 1 − smoothstep(6.8, 7.2, v_lerped), computed per frame. Formation labels: out power2.in 0.4s / in expo.out 0.8s at stage boundaries. IDLE: formation group yaw 0.02 rad/s; clock ticks 1Hz on its own interval; nothing else moves unprovoked — stillness is the luxury here. prefers-reduced-motion: formation morphs become uOpacity cuts, entrances collapse to 0.3s fades, idle yaw off, parallax off.
fallback: Four-rung ladder, each rung designed, none apologetic. RUNG 1 — live WebGL (real GPUs): the full formation gallery, 32 draw calls, dpr ≤ 1.75, IntersectionObserver (<15% visible) + hidden-tab pause. RUNG 2 — designed still path (software renderer detected via WEBGL_debug_renderer_info UNMASKED_RENDERER match on SwiftShader/llvmpipe, OR context creation fails, OR webglcontextlost fires): the poster generator is pure 2D canvas — CPU, it always works — so the stage swaps to a DOM x-strip of the SAME 32 canvases at 180px width, 10px gaps, native horizontal overflow scroll; CSS filter: grayscale(1) reproduces the luminance shader and mask-image: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, black 8%, black 92%, transparent) reproduces fog-to-void at the edges; hover keeps the color reveal via filter: grayscale(0) transition 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (filter, not transform — legal). Contextlost guard: preventDefault, canvas visibility:hidden, rung-2 strip injected from the in-memory poster canvases, one restore attempt on contextrestored. The canvas container's background always equals the current void color — no white flash in Night, no flash at all in White. RUNG 3 — art-directed zero-JS/no-canvas state: hero, hairlines, Index, and Colophon are plain HTML and survive untouched; the stage is a 60vh hairline-framed empty plinth shipped IN the static HTML (removed by JS when rung 1 or 2 boots) with one centered 13px label: `EXHIBIT TEMPORARILY REMOVED FOR CONSERVATION. THE HAIRLINES REMAIN.` — the museum's own move, played straight. RUNG 4 — <1200px: the Gift Shop postcard (see sections), zero WebGL by design, not by failure.
distinct: Monument is the only room in the lab where subtraction is the material: a pure #ffffff/#000000 binary with all layering done by one 0.2-alpha hairline (the hub is warm cream paper with toy-box color chips and 32px radii; Noir is charcoal + bone with a 10px mono-label system and blur chips; Chrome is warm-stone greige with a serif and liquid metal; Pulse is a saturated single red with weight-built hierarchy), ONE typeface at ONE weight doing both the 180px monument and the 13px plaque (every sibling runs the two-family display+workhorse pattern), a brutally binary 94/13px scale with hairlines slicing THROUGH letterforms via margin-top −7px, hand-rolled virtual scroll with Δ·0.002 wheel inertia (the hub and Pulse scroll natively; Noir's pole uses Lenis — ours is the only from-scratch lerp scroll), and an UNLIT ShaderMaterial gallery of 32 seeded-canvas posters — no lights, no shadows, no HDRI, no models — while every sibling world leans on lighting or material response for its 3D. Even its day/night is unmistakable: not a token swap (hub) or a solstice (the Sundial lesson) but a gallery blackout that produces a perfect negative of the same photograph. Screenshot any viewport of this world in grayscale and nothing changes — true of no other page in the lab.
